head: claude/drain-health-backlog-pass3
title: health backlog drain pass 3: retire the diagnostic-provenance class (--all 52 -> 0), and hold it there
body:
## Denominator at base sha `b3772e3a`

**1,100 rows — 524 unresolved** (`open` 337, `kept_open` 187), 565 resolved, 5 superseded, 4 wont_fix, 2 invalid. Measured in-sandbox, matches the brief exactly.

## Burn-down

| | |
|---|--:|
| rows EXAMINED in depth | 6 |
| rows **CLOSED** | **2** |
| rows **REFUSED** | 1 |
| rows **FILED** | 2 |
| **net unresolved** | **524 → 524 (unchanged)** |

**Net unresolved did not move.** Two closed, two filed. Saying that plainly rather than leading with "a class was retired".

## Reconciliation at head — asserted, not trusted

| | base `b3772e3a` | head | arithmetic |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| total | 1100 | **1102** | 1100 + 2 filed ✅ |
| resolved | 565 | **567** | 565 + 2 closed ✅ |
| kept_open | 187 | **185** | 187 − 2 closed ✅ |
| open | 337 | **339** | 337 + 2 filed ✅ |
| superseded / wont_fix / invalid | 5/4/2 | 5/4/2 | unchanged ✅ |

Rows lost **0** · rows invented **0** · duplicate ids **0**. Written through the file's own detected serialisation (`indent=2, ensure_ascii=False`), never by hand — **23 insertions / 6 deletions**, no reformat. `backlog_append.py --check-live`: all 4 live backlogs round-trip byte-for-byte.

## Was there a real class?

**Yes — and it was not one of the three leads as framed.** Lead 1 named *one* row. Probing the 524 for rows whose exit condition names a runnable command found **11 of 524** (confirming the skill's "98% not_checkable"), and among them **two rows share one mechanically-verifiable exit**: drive `scripts/check_diagnostic_provenance.py --all` to zero. That is the class, and unlike a judgement call its closure is a number a command prints.

**52 → 0.** All 52 triaged per site, never mass-annotated (the row's own ASK). Split at the start: D/inert 26 · B/implicit-input 13 · C/unquantified 8 · A/semantic-substitution 5.

- **A (5)** — the label named a quantity the code did not compute. The binary evaluators and the M23 gate now state `predict()` is P(positive) for the binary head they grade and that a `MulticlassPredictor`'s `max(proba)` is not a valid input; `build_research_panel`'s pooled `ms_mean`/`ms_max` now say outright that `score` is not commensurable across heads; `render_system_report` labels the field *logged score = predict()*.
- **B (13)** — every `sorted(glob(...))[-1]` now prints the resolved path **and** the candidate count, on stderr where stdout is a data channel (`gpu_burst/_remote.py` writes `bundle.json` to stdout).
- **C (8)** — the denominator now rides **in the claim**. The sharp one: `scripts/check_writer_conformance.py`, a **CI guard** printing `clean` with no count, so a diff with nothing scannable rendered byte-identical to one fully scanned and clean. Now `clean over N added line(s)` — observed live in this branch's guards run as **`clean over 243 added line(s)`**.
- **D (26)** — fallback stubs and protocol methods marked inert with specific reasons; **two docstrings corrected that claimed an effect the code does not have**; and **three advertised knobs that silently did nothing** now refuse a non-default rather than ignore it.

### Two things that make the zero worth having

1. **The override was cheaper to lie to than to satisfy.** `# inert:` was a bare presence-only regex — the cheapest way to silence a real finding was a comment naming nothing, the `new-table-wiring-guard` failure this repo has already paid for, and one the guard's own test-module docstring *already said must not exist*. It must now **name the parameter**. Tightening it immediately exposed **11 markers across 4 files** that named nothing while the tree reported OK. (All 11 carried genuine reasons — the point is that nothing could tell them from a marker that did not.)
2. **The zero is now held, not just reached.** The guard was diff-scoped, so a site regresses invisibly when an unrelated PR adds the probability-shaped label or deletes the `print` three lines away — which is why the residue sat at **exactly 52 for 26 days across five review passes**. It now carries an **ungated whole-tree `--all` step** (the `api-tier-policy-guard` pattern `run_guards.py` already names as the remedy). That step could not have existed yesterday: it would have failed every PR on day one.

## The two closures

Both closed on **the number the command prints**, never a code citation.

**`BL-20260807-DIAGPROV-STANDING-AUDIT-NEVER-DRAINED`** — criteria asked for ZERO from `--all`.
- **Population:** the guard's declared scope — `scripts/{ml,research,ops,macro,reports}/` + `ml/` + the guard scripts. A **repo** measurement, not a fleet one; the finding is about static code, so the repo is the ground truth. Measured at commit `0dcfcd1e`.
- **Measurement:** `diagnostic-provenance: OK — every scanned diagnostic states what it computed.` (0 findings, from 52).
- **Positive control:** a planted file with one defect per class was caught on **all four** (A, B, C, D); the tree returned to OK once removed. A green that cannot go red proves nothing.

**`BL-20260730-DIAGNOSTIC-PROVENANCE-CLASS`** — two clauses, both met.
- (a) residue zero, as above.
- (b) *"Guard is a required check"* — registered in `scripts/ci/run_guards.py`, riding the `guards` context that `branch-protection-sync.yml` lists in `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`. **Read from the workflow, not assumed.**
- **Positive control** for the guard change: the new regression test **fails on the reverted guard** and passes on the restored one — demonstrated, not asserted.

## The refusal

**`BL-20260813-GUARDS-THAT-TEST-FOR-THE-ABSENCE-OF-A-WRONG-ANSWER`** — has an alternate close reading *"closable when diagnostic-provenance-guard's `--all` reports zero **absence-tests**"*. **Refused.** `--all` reports zero of **its own four classes**; it has no check for `grep -q <literal>` used as an input-provenance test. Reading its zero as an answer about absence-tests would be precisely the **class-A semantic substitution this PR just drained** — a number from one instrument wearing the label of another. Left `kept_open`, untouched.

## Filed (2)

Both are real defects a drain must not silently fix:

- **`BL-20260902-TWO-SIBLING-HF-HARNESSES-DISAGREE-ON-SIGNAL-TTL-SEMANTICS`** — `hf_solo_sim.simulate` implements a real `i - latest_idx >= signal_ttl_bars` expiry; `hf_vectorized.replay` accepted the same parameter, never read it, and hardcodes a 1-bar TTL via `i == pend_idx`. All four call sites use the default, and the default happens to match — so no result so far is wrong. That is luck, not design. `replay` now **raises** on a non-default; reconciling the two engines would change every number the vectorized one has produced, which is a research-semantics decision, not a drain's.
- **`BL-20260902-RECOMBINATION-SWEEP-LABEL-OMITS-ENTRY-KEY-...`** — filed as a **hazard with its precondition named**, not an observed collision.

## Caveats — OBSERVED vs INFERRED

**OBSERVED (measured this session):**
- `--all` 52 → 0; the class split 26/13/8/5; the guard's own OK line.
- The planted-defect positive control firing on all four classes, and the tree returning to OK.
- The strengthened override exposing 11 previously-invisible markers; the new test failing on a reverted guard.
- `writer_conformance: clean over 243 added line(s)` in a real guards run.
- `run_guards.py`: **PASS 67 · FAIL 3**. All three failures are **tooling, not defects** — `pytest` is not installed in this sandbox (2 guards) and `lint-imports` exits 127, command not found (1). **Verified pre-existing**: a clean worktree at base `b3772e3a` fails the same two with the same cause. The affected tests were run directly via a minimal shim: **47 passed, 0 failed** across the 5 files, plus **18 passed, 0 failed** in their class-based suites, plus **29 passed, 0 failed** in the guard's own test module.
- Every touched file parses (`ast.parse`); for `gpu_burst/_remote.py` that is the real proof, since an unbalanced brace in its f-string template would be a SyntaxError.
- Backlog arithmetic and id-set equality at head.

**INFERRED (not measured — check before relying on it):**
- That the three now-refusing knobs change no live behaviour rests on **grep over call sites in-repo**. An external caller passing a non-default would now get an exception instead of a silently wrong number. That is the intended direction, but it is a behaviour change and it is not zero.
- `_build_label`'s collision **hazard**: whether the live pool config actually contains two entry variants sharing a family is **data I did not read**. Filed as a hazard, deliberately not asserted as a bug.
- Docstring corrections (`_label_regime`, `_decay`) rest on reading the bodies, not on running them.
- **39 fixture-dependent test cases could not be run** by the shim (`tmp_path` etc.). They are **UNVERIFIED, not passing**. Real CI has pytest and will run them.
- I did **not** make any live-fleet read. Nothing here needed one — the whole class is static code — but that means nothing in this PR is evidence about the running trader.

## FOR THE MANAGER

- **DRAFT, base `main`, head `claude/drain-health-backlog-pass3`.** Not merged, auto-merge not enabled. Yours.
- **Blast radius:** `scripts/{ml,research,ops,macro,reports}/`, `ml/datasets`, `ml/evaluators`, the guard + its tests, the health backlog, one CLAUDE.md paragraph. **No order-path file, no `config/`, no `ROADMAP.md`, no sibling backlog, no `OPEN-ITEMS.json`.** Nothing touches the live trader.
- **The one judgement call worth your eye:** three research knobs now **raise** instead of silently ignoring their argument. Every in-repo call site uses the default, so today this is inert — but it is the only place I changed behaviour rather than only diagnostics. If you would rather they stayed silent, that is a one-line revert per site.
- **The ungated `--all` guard step is the load-bearing part.** Without it this drain decays exactly as the last one did; with it, a regression fails CI on the PR that causes it. It is also the piece most likely to surprise someone: a PR touching no research script can now fail this guard.
- **CI note:** the 3 red guards are sandbox tooling gaps and are red at base too. Expect green in real CI.
- **Net unresolved is unchanged (524).** The value here is a retired class with a permanent floor under it, not a smaller number.
